summary:
Is a slope-change monitoring map built for the **NASA Space Apps Challenge (Slope Watch)** that turns NASA–ISRO **NISAR** L-band radar data into clear, actionable evidence for mountain communities, guides, and route planners.

 We designed an interactive web mapping prototype powered by Python/GDAL radar processing and an Angular/MapLibre interface. By comparing matched NISAR GCOV scenes and filtering out unreliable pixels with GUNW coherence data, the system flags surface displacement—such as debris slides or glacial lake shifts—using a simple color-coded system (Green for stable, Amber for review, Red when detected change overlaps an active trail or settlement) alongside a separate weather forecast layer

 In high-mountain terrain like the Tian Shan or Himalayas, clouds and darkness frequently block optical satellites, leaving dangerous blind spots between field inspections. Because NISAR’s L-band radar penetrates cloud cover day and night, our tool provides reliable, transparent change evidence—showing exact observation dates, affected areas, and data quality—so local responders can prioritize high-risk routes and prevent disasters before communities are caught off guard.
details:
We built Dancing with Nars for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to help mountain communities, guides, and hikers stay safe from sudden slope changes like debris slides and glacial lake shifts.

Because bad weather and darkness frequently block standard optical satellites in high mountains, we tapped into NASA–ISRO’s NISAR L-band radar, which sees right through clouds day and night. Our backend (Python/GDAL) processes the radar data and feeds an interactive map (Angular/MapLibre) that flags changes using a simple color system—from green (stable) to red (priority review when a hazard intersects a trail).

What sets our project apart is our emphasis on trust and transparency: we filter out unreliable radar shadows, clearly label missing coverage as "unknown," and separate hard radar evidence from weather forecasts. We’re kicking off our first pilot in the Tian Shan mountains, working hand-in-hand with local rescue teams and guides.
